text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. speaker: Doctor
text: The history of self-resolving knee pain followed by wrist pain, fever, and chills after a trip to Minnesota is highly concerning for Lyme disease or disseminated gonococcal infection. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI).

The clinical picture of a sexually active young male with a history of transient arthritis (knee), followed by a septic arthritis (wrist), fever, and a migrating skin rash is classic for DGI. Given the Minnesota trip, Lyme disease is less likely to present with this specific triad of self-resolving arthritis and acute septic arthritis of a different joint. The requested labs (CBC, CRP, ESR, VDRL/RPR) will likely show leukocytosis and negative syphilis serology. I have already ordered the necessary tests; pending culture results from the wrist joint aspiration or blood cultures, I will proceed with empiric treatment for gonococcal infection.
